Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list. Quick overview up front, then I’ll push the DPA/subprocessor bundle from Legal.

- Subprocessors: For Private (VPC) deployments we only use a small set of subprocessors for control-plane services (billing, customer portal, metrics ingestion) — they do NOT receive decrypted customer request payloads. For on-prem/air-gapped installs we run with zero-control-plane subprocessors by default. I’ll attach the latest CSV.
- Customer KMS: Yes, we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via standard KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) and HSMs for on-prem. When BYOK is enabled, Redwood never stores plaintext model input/output keys; we use envelope encryption patterns. Key rotation is supported — operations require a validated handoff but do not expose plaintext to Redwood personnel.
- Operator access: Our default model is metadata-only access for normal ops. Breakglass is tightly audited and requires two-person approval from the customer-designated escalation contacts and a Redwood SRE. Even in breakglass, we only accept a customer-provided ephemeral unwrap token to decrypt session artifacts — Redwood staff do not retain master key material.
- Telemetry/cross-border: By default, minimal telemetry (errors, latency, token counts) is sent to the control plane in the selected region. For regulated customers we can disable telemetry export and provide on-prem observability agents. The DPA has the transfer/processing clauses and we can add an explicit annex for telemetry retention local-only.

I’ll let Marissa & Rishi drop the legal/tech specifics and the DPA + subprocessor list. Proposed next step: 30-min runbook/architecture call (Tom + your infra + me + Marissa) tomorrow. What time works?

Best,
Jordan
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

Highlights below you can cite to procurement: 

- Data access model: For Private VPC deployments, customer data-plane traffic is routed through customer-managed networking. Control-plane telemetry is limited to non-content metrics unless you opt in. On-prem installs default to zero external processors.
- KMS & key custody: We support Customer-Managed Keys (BYOK). In Private VPC we integrate customer KMS via key-wrapping. Redwood does not store plaintext keys; unwrap operations require either ephemeral customer approval or an HSM escrow key (if customer elects). The DPA Annex includes a keystore responsibility matrix.
- Subprocessors: List includes (examples): LogMetrics Inc (metrics pipeline — receives anonymized metrics), DocTrust (DocuSign processing for contracts), and CloudCarrier (billing). None of the listed subprocessors have access to unencrypted request or response payloads for Private VPC. The CSV has contact & jurisdiction columns for each.
- Breakglass & operator procedures: We documented a two-person approval workflow and an audit trail retention policy (90 days by default, extendable). We will add your requirement for PoLP (principle of least privilege) and an on-call roster export for audits.

If Medexa requires, we can add an explicit clause that Redwood will accept breakglass only via a customer-provided ephemeral unwrap token or via a documented legal escrow process — we can add both options as contract addenda.

We can take comments directly on the PDF (please use the DocuSign/Drive link) or propose language edits and our contracts team will produce a redline. Jordan — I’m available 13:00–16:00 PT for the runbook call.

Tom/Sarah — quick answers and next steps before the 15:00 PT call: 

1) KMS key policies: Yes — we support configurations where the customer KMS key policy explicitly denies Redwood IAM Decrypt by default. Our integration uses envelope keys and the unwrap call can be gated by a short-lived principal or by acceptance of a signed, customer-provided token. We’ll surface a recommended key-policy template in the runbook.
2) Healthchecks/heartbeats: Agent heartbeats contain only service health metadata (uptime, version, sequence ID). They do NOT contain request/response payloads or PHI/PII by default. For additional assurance, we can route heartbeats over a customer-only telemetry pipe or disable them entirely.

Call: 15:00 PT works for us. Agenda: 1) Confirm BYOK key-policy template & rotation flow; 2) Walk the breakglass log flow & audit; 3) Identify any DPA redlines; 4) Kick off procurement checklist. I’ll send a calendar invite and include the DocuSign/Drive links for the DPA.
